newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica, PNC Bank net income rise on quarter.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica, PNC Bank net income rise on quarter.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp., the nation's third largest bank, said Wednesday that its profits grew by 11 percent in the second quarter, boosted in part by consumer loan growth in the improving California market.
San Francisco-based BankAmerica reported net income climbed to $799 million during the quarter, compared with $723 million in the same period a year ago.
Earnings per share rose to $1.07, from 92 cents a share a year ago. The per-share results reflect a two-for-one stock split on June 2.

"Clearly, there is steady growth in the rest of the franchise, but California is particularly noticeable because of the absence of growth for a number of years as it recovers from the recession and essentially restructure the economy," said BankAmerica Chief Financial Officer Mike O'Neill in a conference call. "The trend is clear."
Non-interest net income rose 9 percent, to $122 million. The growth included an $84 million increase in fees and commissions, primarily due to higher loan-servicing fees.
BankAmerica's stock closed up $2.50 at $69.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
"It was a very solid quarter," said Gerard Klauer Mattison analyst George Salem.

Meanwhile, the stock price of San Francisco-based Wells Fargo and Co. fell $4.125 to $262.875 as analysts slashed forecasts Wednesday, one day after Wells reported disappointing second-quarter results and operating losses due to continued troubles in integrating First Interstate Bancorp.

"Management states that the astonishing operating losses are well controlled with the worst behind them ... but we are quite concerned about the losses of customer deposits and loan balances which have yet to be arrested at Wells," Salem said.
Indeed, O'Neill said BankAmerica has picked up some of Wells Fargo's lost business.

"We have renewed emphasis on customer service, and I think we're beginning to see some beneficial impact. We are not distracted," BankAmerica's O'Neill said, adding, "When you do big mergers, there is no question that you are consumed by many things and custonmer service takes a back seat."
O'Neill said the bank's credit quality continues to improve with non-accrual assets at historic lows, representing one-half of 1 percent of the bank's total loans.
"The only negative in the credit story is credit cards, which continue to suffer principally from the bankruptcy phenomenon which is occurring in the U.S.," he said.

Nevertheless, O'Neill said BankAmerica intends to expand this sector, which is a relatively small business for the company. On a managed basis, BankAmerica has just under $10 billion in credit card receivables outstanding, he said.

Pittsburgh-based PNC Bank Corp. said its second-quarter net income rose 4 percent to $259 million, vs. $248 million in the second quarter of 1996. Earnings per share rose to 81 cents, from 72 cents a share a year ago, matching analysts' expectations.

PNC reported its non-interest income jumped 29 percent on the year. It said non-interest income in the second quarter rose to $433.4 million, from $336.6 million a year ago, boosted by strong growth in fee-based businesses.
Fee-based revenue rose 21 percent, led by gains in its asset management, private banking, treasury management and capital markets sectors, the company said.

"These businesses are among the growth opportunities we have been pursuing for some time that are now making a more meaningful contribution to our financial performance," PNC Chairman Thomas O'Brien said in a statement.
PNC rose $1 to $43.375 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.

Portland, Ore.-based U.S. Bancorp's net income fell to $125.6 million in the second quarter from $127.1 million in the same year-ago period. Earnings per share rose to 83 cents, matching analysts' forecasts, from 82 cents a year ago.

Seattle-based Washington Mutual Inc. announced record second-quarter earnings of $118.8 million, an increase of 19 percent, from earnings of $99.6 million a year earlier. Earnings per share rose to 96 cents, from 85 cents a share in the same year-ago period, slightly less than analysts expectations for 95 cents.
